scope: Six titles and complete activity instructions; not background curriculum or child-use approval.

strings.U6-L01-step-1: Caregiver claps once and draws one mark on the paper; count aloud in the home language: one, two, three.
strings.U6-L01-step-2: Touch each dot and count them again together; repeat while the child enjoys it — repetition is the point, not an error.
strings.U6-L01-step-3: Child claps, caregiver draws the marks; then swap. Caregiver counts along without correcting mid-count.
strings.U6-L01-step-4: New small group (2, then 4 claps): 'How many now?' Accept pointing at dots, saying a number, or re-drawing as full answers.
strings.U6-L01-step-5: Magic fold: fold the paper, open, count again — or stop warmly whenever the child is done; stopping early is a success.
strings.U6-L02-step-1: During feeding or dressing: when the baby makes a sound or movement, respond with a short phrase in your language and pause, waiting as if the baby will answer.
strings.U6-L02-step-2: During play: copy the baby's sound once, then add one real word for it (ba-ba, then 'bottle' in your language).
strings.U6-L02-step-3: Evening, without the child: answer the card's two questions to yourself — what did my child 'say' today, what did I say back? Nothing is written into any app; an optional private paper note is fine.
strings.B-L01-step-1: Oral entry (L0): facilitator reads the message aloud twice; learner says or shows what to bring (mime, pointing to a real pencil/notebook, or speech).
strings.B-L01-step-2: L1-L2: read the message; answer 'What do you bring?' by pointing to the exact words first, then saying the answer.
strings.B-L01-step-3: Second question: 'What time does it start?' Learner points to the time words, answers, and shows how they know — pointing is the accepted proof.
strings.B-L01-step-4: Transfer: facilitator writes a brand-new one-line message ('Bring two pencils.'); learner answers and points to the evidence — or uses the oral route on a new spoken message.
strings.B-L01-step-5: Close: learner folds the card into a letter and delivers/retells it to a family member. Real reading purpose; no scoring.
strings.B-L02-step-1: Tell the story: Nwe and two friends picked 12 mangoes (paper tokens) and want a fair share. Learners cut or tear 12 tokens.
strings.B-L02-step-2: Deal tokens one-by-one into three drawn circles. Foundational: deal then count each circle. Developing: predict first, then deal to check.
strings.B-L02-step-3: Say or show the answer and how they know (dealing order, counting runs, '3 fours'). All modes accepted.
strings.B-L02-step-4: Transfer with new numbers: 10 tokens and 2 friends (foundational) or 15 tokens and 3 friends, then 'what if one more friend comes?' (developing; remainder idea, no division algorithm expected).
strings.B-L02-step-5: Close: write or draw the number story (12 to 3 groups of 4, or a picture); it goes into the private portfolio only if the learner chooses.
strings.A-L01-step-1: Hand out both cards (read-aloud support for anyone, no stigma). Ask: what is different about these two texts? Expected: Card A names an issuer and a date; Card B is unattributed hearsay.
strings.A-L01-step-2: Foundation: 'On which days does the van come according to Card A?' Answer and point to or read the exact line — the pointing is the point.
strings.A-L01-step-3: Extension: 'Can these two cards tell you whether the van comes on Saturday?' Explain: Card B is unattributed hearsay; Card A is silent on Saturday; the cards cannot settle it — checking Card A's issuing source is the next step.
strings.A-L01-step-4: Transfer: 'Your neighbour asks when the van comes. What do you say, based on which card?' The answer must cite the source, not only the fact.
strings.A-L01-step-5: Close: two-minute pair/family share — one thing you would check before forwarding a message like Card B. No real messages brought into the room.
strings.A-L02-step-1: Find the arrival time when leaving Padauk Road at 7:30 — trace the column with a finger (Foundation) or use the picture-row cards (non-reading entry). Answer: 8:15.
strings.A-L02-step-2: Extension: 'You must be at Hill Market by 8:00. Which departure works — and what does the table NOT tell you?' Expected: 6:10; no information about delays, Sunday service or fare.
strings.A-L02-step-3: Practise the Thai phrase twice: choral with the facilitator, then individually — reading, whispering or saying it; pointing at the phrase card instead of speaking is accepted this week. Home-language meaning is given orally by the facilitator until a reviewed home-language gloss exists (a prior machine gloss was withdrawn for a known mistranslation of 'market').
strings.A-L02-step-4: Transfer: 'You are at Old Gate at 7:50. What do you do?' Reading the table (9:05) or forming the question to ask at the counter — either is success; both is stronger.
strings.A-L02-step-5: Close: write one thing the table cannot tell you, on paper, for the private portfolio (the learner chooses to keep or bin it).
